steps.message:
# Report support SLA breaches

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service, which you can use through the `tickets` MCP server.

The support SLA policy is kept in the open ticket labeled `sla-policy`. Apply it to every ticket it covers, measured up to now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC, and find the tickets that breached their first-response target, their resolution target, or both.

1. Add exactly one comment to each breached ticket, with the text `SLA breach: <metrics>`, where `<metrics>` is `first-response`, `resolution`, or `first-response, resolution`. A ticket that already has a comment starting with `SLA breach:` was reported by an earlier review: do not comment on it again.
2. Create one ticket that reports the review:
   - title: `SLA breach report 2026-09-14`
   - team: `support-ops`
   - priority: `P2`
   - labels: `sla-report`
   - body: one line per breached ticket, including those reported by an earlier review, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id> <metrics>`, and nothing else

Do not change the status or priority of any ticket, and do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":815,\"title\":\"Support SLA policy\",\"body\":\"Support SLA policy, revision 2026-06, in force since 2026-07-01.\\n\\nScope: every ticket with the label `sla`, whatever its status.\\n\\nBusiness hours: Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00 UTC. Holidays without business hours: 2026-09-07.\\nOnly business time counts toward a target.\\n\\nTargets in business hours:\\n- P1: first response 1h, resolution 8h\\n- P2: first response 4h, resolution 16h\\n- P3: first response 8h, resolution 40h\\n- P4: first response 16h, resolution 80h\\n\\nFirst response: the business time from creation to the first comment by a support agent. Support agents comment under a staff handle without `@` (for example `s.ortiz`). Comments by the customer and by `helpdesk` are not responses.\\n\\nResolution: the business time during which the status was `open`, from creation until the ticket was last set to `resolved` or `closed`. The clock stops while the status is `pending` (waiting on the customer). When a resolved ticket is reopened, the clock continues from where it stopped; the time it spent resolved does not count.\\n\\nPriority: each target uses the priority in force when the metric was met (the first response; the last resolution). For a metric not met yet, the current priority applies.\\n\\nBreach: a metric is breached when its business time is greater than its target. A metric not met yet is breached when its business time up to now is already greater than its target.\\n\\n`helpdesk` records every change as a comment: `status: <old> -> <new>` or `priority: <old> -> <new>`. A ticket is created with status `open`; its first priority is the one before its first priority change.\\n\",\"status\":\"open\",\"priority\":\"P4\",\"team\":\"support-ops\",\"customer\":\"ops@example.com\",\"labels\":[\"sla-policy\"],\"created_at\":\"2026-09-01T08:00:00Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-01T08:00:00Z\",\"comments\":[]}"}

steps.message:
I applied the SLA policy (#815) to the 28 tickets labeled `sla`, found 12 in breach, and finished all the steps. The breach calls come from my own business-hours arithmetic, not from a tool, so they're worth a spot-check.

- **Comments:** I added `SLA breach: <metrics>` to 11 tickets: #804, #806, #808, #810, #816, #818, #820, #826, #829, #832 and #836.
- **Report:** I created ticket #837, "SLA breach report 2026-09-14" (team `support-ops`, P2, label `sla-report`). It lists all 12 breached tickets in id order.
- **#824:** An earlier review already commented `SLA breach: first-response`, so I added no comment. It also breached resolution, so its report line reads `first-response, resolution`.
- **#823:** An earlier review commented `SLA breach: resolution`, but by my calculation it was not in breach (17.5 business hours against a 40-hour P3 target). I left it out of the report and did not comment.

I changed no statuses or priorities and touched no other tickets. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.
